prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) enforces permissives/interlocks, timestamps changes, provides bay indications, sends Bay Status Digest→Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing). Glasswing separates indications/communications-quality from evidence, retains cleared-alarm states/events, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller have non-substitutable scopes; north blocks unready closes. Breaker Control Unit executes only permitted commands; control failure cannot inhibit protection. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects feeders, produces Relay Diagnostic Note. North Protection Panel contains feeder protection equipment/indications; Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformers, provides local operation indications. Station Gateway brokers authorized control-room/bay traffic using configured mappings/addressing/access-controls; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Supervisory requests, bay execution, protection remain separate despite layer loss. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) produces Clock Drift Snapshot→Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), authoritative time-ordered evidence. Engineering Workstation provides authorized revision-controlled review/export/configuration, produces Settings Review Receipt; never substitutes immediate assessment. Maintenance Remote Terminal grants approved access, not local authority. Station DC System powers automation/protection, produces retained Battery Load Test Record.
Control Room Operator requests switching; reviews alarms before acknowledgement; records response/outstanding actions on slip; checks bay/device/sequence, feeder/protection, transformer and DC indications. Cleared indications do not prove correction; breaker discrepancies remain abnormal pending understanding. Operator produces Clearance Handoff Memo for unresolved-alarm handoff; verifies alarm/equipment/evidence consistency before closure. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) checks conflicts/clearances, produces Isolation Boundary Card, confirms handback before engineering evidence review. Substation Supervisor authorizes/escalates. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) interprets settings/diagnostics/events. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies identity/conditions before authorized operations; sends Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time).
Requirements: bounded authority, coordinated boundaries/shared equipment; ordered switching/holds/stops, local/interlock precedence; communications-loss stale displays/work-stop/verified recovery; time never controls protection; preserve source/order/time/quality, flag uncertainty/corrections; authorized quality-preserving queries/exports; auditable administration/retention/holds/capacity/ingestion/recovery/tested backups; coordinated settings revision, independent approval, model/firmware checks, installation comparison/testing/discrepancy-resolution; post-handback review.

New part:
S173: It rejects malformed, stale, or unauthorized requests and records each rejection with enough context for operations review.
S174: Station Supervisory Control System presents available controls and indications to authorized operating personnel.
S175: Control Room Operator issues state-changing requests only through approved operating procedures and the configured supervisory interface.
S176: Bay Automation Controller validates each received request against local mode, interlocks, command authority, and equipment availability before issuing bay-level outputs.
S177: Breaker Control Unit applies accepted output commands at the breaker interface and returns the resulting position and circuit-health indications.
S178: Bay Automation Controller compares returned indications with the requested state and identifies incomplete or contradictory operation.
S179: Bay Automation Controller uses the inspection tag to associate the applicable equipment context with an authorized record.
S180: Station Gateway carries updated indications through the station interface using configured quality and timestamp attributes.
S181: Station Supervisory Control System displays indication quality and stale-data status so operators can distinguish a current value from a retained value.
S182: Sequence Event Archive retains time-tagged changes and control outcomes for event reconstruction and operational review.
S183: Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time reference used to align event timestamps, subject to configured quality checks.
S184: Bay Automation Controller monitors communication health and places affected points in a defined degraded state when updates exceed configured age limits.
S185: Station Gateway reports link condition and protocol errors without converting a communication failure into an equipment-state change.
S186: Tandem evaluates electrical quantities against approved settings and issues protective trip outputs without relying on supervisory communications.
S187: North Protection Panel applies its assigned zone logic and maintains trip paths independently of supervisory network availability.
S188: Transformer Protection Panel applies its assigned protective logic and reports abnormal protection conditions through its configured interface.
S189: North Bay Controller maintains local bay control within the approved operating mode when supervisory communications are interrupted.
S190: South Bay Controller reports local mode and control availability through its configured bay interface.
S191: Engineering Workstation supports approved configuration review and does not serve as a routine source of operating commands.
S192: Maintenance Remote Terminal access is restricted to authorized maintenance sessions and is not used to bypass local interlocks.
S193: Station DC System supports control and protection functions through monitored station supply circuits, and supply loss is indicated as an abnormal station condition.
S194: Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection event records and verifies that approved settings remain consistent with coordination requirements.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
